source_title: Prince William to sell 20% of $1.3B Duchy to fund housing projects
source_excerpt: Prince William is using one of the British royal family's most valuable assets to pursue causes close to his heart, with plans to sell a portion of his vast estate to fund housing, environmental recovery and renewable energy projects.The Prince of Wales, 44, took control of the Duchy of Cornwall after the death of his grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, in September 2022. The estate, which spans more than 128,000 acres, is valued at over $1.3 billion and provides William with an annual private income of nearly $31 million.However, the future king is looking beyond the traditional role of the estate as a source of income. According to a report by The Times, William plans to sell around 20% of the Duchy's assets, potentially raising an estimated $670 million to support a new approach centred on social needs, nature recovery and clean energy.Why Prince William wants to reshape the Duchy of CornwallEstablished in 1337, the Duchy of Cornwall was created to provide an income for the heir to the British throne and support the household and public responsibilities associated with the role. It has traditionally consisted of land, property and other assets managed on behalf of the heir apparent.William inherited control of the estate when his father, King Charles III, became monarch following Queen Elizabeth II's death. When William eventually becomes king, control will pass to his eldest son, Prince George, continuing the centuries-old tradition.Under William's leadership, however, the estate is being encouraged to take a more active role in addressing local challenges. The reported plan to sell a fifth of its assets would allow it to focus its resources on five key areas, including Cornwall, Dartmoor, the Isles of Scilly, Bath and parts of London.Duchy chief executive Will Bax has outlined a vision in which the organisation evaluates its presence according to the positive impact it can deliver."If we donât see an opportunity for positive impact, then perhaps we donât need to be a part of that place," Bax told The Times."But where there is social need and where there is environmental challenge and where there is an opportunity to enable change, then weâll be a great partner in working with people to achieve that."The approach reflects William's broader interest in using his position and resources to address social and environmental concerns.Tackling homelessness through housing projectsOne of William's priorities for the Duchy is addressing homelessness, an issue he has also made central to his wider Homewards initiative.The project seeks to develop practical, locally driven solutions to homelessness, bringing together organisations and communities to explore ways of preventing people from losing their homes.In 2024, Ben Murphy, estate director at the Duchy of Cornwall, explained that William had asked the estate to address homelessness in Cornwall and other areas where it operates."As one of his key priorities for the Duchy of Cornwall, Prince William asked us to address the homelessness challenge within Cornwall and other areas where the estate resides," Murphy said.The Duchy is already developing social housing in Nansledan, near Newquay in Cornwall. The project is part of a broader effort to create communities that combine housing with local services and commercial spaces.Another planned development on Market Street in Newquay aims to create a new high street featuring independent businesses, local artisans and community enterprises. The project is expected to be completed in 2028 and is intended to help strengthen the local economy.These developments illustrate how the estate's property portfolio could be used to support communities beyond its traditional financial role.Why William is redirecting money from Dartmoor PrisonThe Prince of Wales has also taken steps to redirect income from an estate asset that is no longer being used for its original purpose.Dartmoor Prison, which has remained empty since July 2024, had generated approximately $2 million a year in rental income for William. Rather than continue to retain that money, he directed that the annual amount be returned to the local community through the Princetown Community Fund.According to a September press release, the fund will support projects delivering lasting social, economic and environmental benefits for people in Princetown and the surrounding Dartmoor area.The decision aligns with the wider direction of the Duchy under William: ensuring that assets and income are connected to the needs of the communities in which the estate operates.Princess Kate's early childhood initiative finds a partner in the DuchyWilliam's plans also intersect with the work of his wife, Princess Kate, particularly her focus on early childhood development and the role of nature in children's well-being.Kate's Centre for Early Childhood has partnered with the Duchy of Cornwall to explore how time spent outdoors can support the mental well-being and development of young children, as well as the people who care for them.The collaboration, launched in Nansledan, examines how nature, creativity and relationships can help children develop the social and emotional skills that contribute to lifelong health and well-being."This project is about exploring how nature, creativity and relationships can best support the healthy development of babies and young children," Kate said in a video."We believe that taking a whole-child approach is important, and nature becomes a wonderful place to explore how we can successfully nurture the social and emotional skills that underpin lifelong health and wellbeing."The initiative connects the Duchy's environmental ambitions with Kate's long-standing interest in the early years of childhood, highlighting how the estate's land can be used for projects that benefit families and local communities.Cornwall remains important to William and his familyIn addition to fulfilling its financial obligations and executing various public initiatives, the Duchy of Cornwall maintains a significant personal connection to the family life of Prince William and Catherine, the Princess of Wales.The Duchy encompasses Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, both of which are cherished locations where the royal family enjoys spending quality time together.
